tasks.subject: [flow-usage] [P1] Map status-line, transcript and rate_limit_event readings to ledger observations, test-first
tasks.description:
Blocked by flow-cli-core tasks 1.1 (fleet/accounts.ts, fleet/usage-ledger.ts, atomic-json.ts) and 1.5 (flow.ts) being merged. Add two zero-dependency modules under plugins/flow/scripts/fleet/ that import no npm package.

(a) fleet/observations.ts, all pure:
- fromStatusLine(payload, now): for each key of payload.rate_limits matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ whose value is an object with a finite number used_percentage, emit {key, usedPct: clamp(used_percentage, 0, 100), resetsAt: toIso(resets_at), status: null, observedAt: now ISO UTC, source: 'statusline'}. toIso: a number is epoch SECONDS; a string goes through Date.parse; missing or invalid -> null. A window without a numeric used_percentage is skipped (the ledger needs usedPct or status, and the status line gives no status). No rate_limits -> [].
- fromTranscriptEntry(entry): only when entry.isApiErrorMessage === true, entry.error === 'rate_limit' and entry.timestamp parses. Window key = entry.quotaLimits.rateLimitType when it is a string matching the window-key pattern; else from the first message.content text block: /session limit/ -> five_hour, /weekly limit/ -> seven_day; else return {unidentified: true} (model-limit texts such as "You've reached your Fable limit" are never recorded: with no reset they would read as rejected for 7 days under the stale rule). usedPct null; resetsAt = quotaLimits.resetsAt (epoch seconds, finite number) as ISO, else parseResetText(text, observedAt, key), else null; status 'rejected'; observedAt = timestamp as ISO UTC; source 'transcript'.
- fromRateLimitEvent(info, observedAt): the contract sdk_event row. key = rateLimitType (skip when absent or failing the pattern), usedPct = utilization * 100 clamped (null when utilization absent), resetsAt from epoch seconds, status as given, source 'sdk_event'; skip when both usedPct and status are null.
- parseResetText(text, observedAt, key): regex `resets (?:(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) (\d{1,2}) at )?(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?(am|pm) \(([^)]+)\)`. Zone = the IANA name in parentheses; Intl RangeError -> null. With a date: that wall time in that zone in the year of observedAt (in that zone); if the result is more than 1 day before observedAt use the next year. Without a date: the first instant strictly after observedAt whose wall time in the zone matches. Wall time -> instant via Intl.DateTimeFormat offsets, re-checked once for DST; a repeated wall time (fall back) takes the EARLIER instant; a non-existent one (spring forward) -> null. Sanity bound: result must be after observedAt and at most window length + 1 h later (five_hour 6 h, seven_day 7 d 1 h), else null.

(b) fleet/config-dir.ts: defaultConfigDir(env, osHome) = CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when set and non-empty else <osHome>/.claude; accountForConfigDir(identities, dir): expand leading ~, path.resolve, drop trailing separator, compare fs.realpathSync.native of both sides (fallback to the resolved path when realpath throws); rows whose id fails ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ never match; first match in registry order wins; no match -> null.

Fixtures (made-up ids and paths only) in engine-tests/fixtures/usage/: statusline/{full.json (both windows, epoch resets_at), iso-resets.json, no-rate-limits.json, partial.json (seven_day without used_percentage), extra-window.json (seven_day_opus), bad-values.json (a string, 140, -5, a key failing the pattern), pretty.json (multi-line), not-json.txt}; transcripts/{structured.jsonl (a quotaLimits five_hour hit and a seven_day hit shaped like a Claude Code 2.1.280 entry: type assistant, message.model '<synthetic>', content [{type:'text', text:"You've hit your session limit · resets 3:30pm (America/Chicago)"}], quotaLimits {status:'rejected', resetsAt, rateLimitType}, error 'rate_limit', isApiErrorMessage true, apiErrorStatus 429, timestamp), text-only.jsonl (the session text with a time; "You've hit your weekly limit · resets Sep 18 at 3pm (America/Chicago)"; the weekly text with no date), model-limit.jsonl ("You've reached your Fable limit. Switch to another model…"), decoy.jsonl (a user message quoting \"error\":\"rate_limit\"; an ordinary assistant line), broken.jsonl (a torn line between two hits)}.

Tests (engine-tests/usage/observations.test.ts, config-dir.test.ts), each with a purpose comment and shown to fail against a broken implementation: every statusline fixture maps to the exact observations; structured quotaLimits beats text; text classification; model-limit and decoy produce nothing; parseResetText time-only rolling past midnight, date with year rollover (observed Dec 30, resets Jan 2), the repeated 01:30 on 2026-11-01 America/Chicago takes the earlier instant, 02:30 on 2027-03-14 America/Chicago gives null, unknown zone null, out-of-bound null; accountForConfigDir unset env -> ~/.claude, trailing slash, symlinked dir matches its target, invalid-id row never matches, first of two matches wins. Acceptance: tests pass, both modules import no npm package, typecheck and prettier clean.

tasks.subject: [flow-usage] [P1] Build the session registry: Claude Code session files, DorkOS sessions and flow runs joined on sessionId
tasks.description:
Blocked by flow-cli-core tasks 1.1 and 1.4 (the FlowRun file reader) being merged. Add plugins/flow/scripts/fleet/sessions.ts, zero npm dependencies, all I/O injected (fs root, process runner, fetch, now) so it is unit-testable.

- readCliSessions(identities, deps): for each identity with a valid id, every <path>/sessions/*.json (not recursive). A file needs a number pid and a string sessionId; cwd, status, startedAt (epoch ms), procStart, name optional; anything else is skipped with a warning. Alive = process.kill(pid, 0) succeeds or throws EPERM; then ONE `ps -o pid=,lstart= -p <pid,...>` call: a pid whose lstart text differs from procStart (when both exist) was reused and counts as dead; if ps fails the kill check stands. Dead sessions are dropped. Account = that identity's id.
- fetchDorkosSessions(url, deps): refuse (throw a usage error, exit 2 at the CLI) unless the URL host is 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1. GET <url>/api/sessions?limit=500 with a 1.5 s timeout. Connection refused -> {reachable:false}; non-2xx -> {reachable:true, warning:'DorkOS answered <status>'}; 2xx -> keep sessions that have a `status` object or whose trackerItem.runStatus is queued, running or waiting_for_review; reportsLive = whether any session on the page carried a `status` or `trackerItem` field. Account = accountId, else the identity whose path equals `account` (path.resolve equality), else null. Default url resolution (for the CLI): --dorkos-url, else FLOW_DORKOS_URL, else http://127.0.0.1:<DORKOS_PORT or 4242>.
- collectRuns(cwds, deps): main checkout of each distinct cwd = parent of `git -C <cwd> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` (at most 8 at once, 2 s timeout each, failure = none); read each <main>/.dork/flow/flow-state.json with S1's reader, no lock; unreadable -> warning; keep runs with status queued, running or waiting_for_review.
- joinSessions(cli, dorkos, runs, ledgerByAccount, now): join on sessionId. A session matching a run takes item = run.identifier, stage = run.stage, host = run.host when set. The same sessionId from CLI and DorkOS is one row, DorkOS fields winning and host dorkos unless the run says otherwise. A run matched by no session is its own row (account = run.account or null, host = run.host or null). Unlinked host: CLI -> cli, DorkOS -> dorkos. Each row lists its sources ('claude-code' | 'dorkos' | 'flow-run').
- sessionState(row, ...): DorkOS: status.limit set -> limited; lifecycle streaming -> busy, blocked -> parked, idle -> idle, error and interrupted as is. Claude Code: status busy -> busy, idle -> idle, other values as is, missing -> unknown. Run-only: waiting_for_review -> parked; workerPid present and not alive -> stale; else unseen. Override: an idle row whose account's five_hour or seven_day reads rejected now via readWindow (not expired) -> limited; the override never replaces busy.
- Sort: account registry order (unknown last), then item, then startedAt.

Fixtures in engine-tests/fixtures/usage/: sessions/ (busy, idle, shell, a dead pid, a reused pid via procStart mismatch, one missing sessionId), dorkos/ (a GET /api/sessions body with accountId, status {lifecycle, limit} and trackerItem {id, stage, runStatus}; one from a release without them), flow-state.json (running, waiting_for_review, complete, and runs linked to the fixture session ids).

Tests (engine-tests/fleet/sessions.test.ts): every row of the state table; the idle-only override; liveness incl. pid reuse and ps failure; DorkOS refused / 401 / pre-D7 body / non-loopback refusal; a session serving an item shows it; CLI + DorkOS duplicate collapses; run-only rows. Acceptance: tests pass, zero npm imports, typecheck and prettier clean.

tasks.subject: [flow-usage] [P2] Ship flow usage record and the background status-line hook
tasks.description:
Add plugins/flow/scripts/cli/usage.ts (the `usage` verb: dispatches record | scan | probe | install-statusline by dynamic import(); no sub-verb or an unknown one prints the list to stderr and exits 2) and cli/usage-record.ts, registered in flow.ts's verb table.

`flow usage record [--account <id>] [--verbose] [--json]`:
- stdin: read at most 1 MiB (more: record nothing, exit 0). stdin is a TTY: print 'pipe the status-line JSON in; see flow usage --help' to stderr, exit 2.
- Account: --account, else accountForConfigDir(identities, defaultConfigDir(env, osHome)). No match: exit 0, nothing written.
- observations = fromStatusLine(JSON.parse(stdin), now); unparsable JSON or none -> exit 0.
- One call to S1's ledger writer (mergeLedger under the lock, gives up after 2 s without throwing). A 3 s watchdog (unref'd timer) exits 0 whatever is happening.
- Dedupe stamp: when FLOW_USAGE_STAMP and FLOW_USAGE_FP are set and the writer did not give up, write FLOW_USAGE_FP + newline to FLOW_USAGE_STAMP via temp + rename, mode 0600, but ONLY if its parent is exactly <dorkHome>/usage and its basename starts with .statusline- (otherwise ignore it). A dropped write leaves the stamp alone.
- Default mode prints nothing to stdout ever; stderr only with --verbose; exit 0 except TTY/argv errors (2). --json prints {v:1, ok:true, account, recorded:[keys], changed, dropped}.
- The whole record path (flow.ts -> cli/usage.ts -> cli/usage-record.ts -> fleet/observations.ts, fleet/config-dir.ts, fleet/accounts.ts, fleet/usage-ledger.ts, atomic-json.ts) imports no npm package.

Ship plugins/flow/scripts/usage/statusline-hook.sh, git mode 0755, bash 3.2 compatible, builtins only until node:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# flow usage recorder. A status-line script runs this in the background.
# It prints nothing and always exits 0. See docs/account-usage.mdx.
IFS= read -r -d '' input || true
case $input in *'"rate_limits"'*) ;; *) exit 0 ;; esac
fp=${input#*'"rate_limits"'}; fp=${fp%%'}}'*}
dir=${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}
stamp=${DORK_HOME:-$HOME/.dork}/usage/.statusline-${dir//[^A-Za-z0-9]/_}
last=; [ -r "$stamp" ] && IFS= read -r last < "$stamp"
[ "$fp" = "$last" ] && exit 0
here=${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}
printf '%s' "$input" | FLOW_USAGE_FP="$fp" FLOW_USAGE_STAMP="$stamp" \
  "${FLOW_NODE:-node}" --experimental-strip-types "$here/../flow.ts" usage record >/dev/null 2>&1
exit 0
```
The two lines a status-line script gets, right after its `<var>=$(cat)` line:
```bash
# flow usage recorder (opt-in): records this account's usage for `flow fleet`. See <flow-root>/docs/account-usage.mdx
[ -x '<abs hook path>' ] && { printf '%s' "$<var>" | FLOW_NODE='<abs node path>' '<abs hook path>'; } >/dev/null 2>&1 &
```

Tests (engine-tests/usage/record.test.ts and record-process.test.ts), each with a purpose comment and shown to fail against a broken implementation: record writes five_hour and seven_day WITH resetsAt from the full fixture and stdout is empty (DOR-2369 validation 1); an unregistered dir, bad JSON and a TTY write nothing; a dropped write (lock held by a live holder past 2 s) leaves the stamp unwritten; a stamp path outside <dorkHome>/usage is ignored; --json envelope. Process tests with real bash and node: (1) NOT BLOCKING: a status-line script containing the two lines, whose hook path points to a script that sleeps 2 s, returns its output in under 50 ms when run the way Claude Code runs it (stdout captured through a pipe until EOF); (2) DEDUPE under a temp DORK_HOME with FLOW_NODE pointing at a stub that counts calls then execs real node: first payload starts record and the stamp appears, the same payload again does not start it, a changed used_percentage starts it again; run with /bin/bash (3.2 on macOS) and the CI bash; (3) ZERO DEPS: `usage record` run from a copy of scripts/ with no node_modules writes the ledger. Report median and p95 wall time of `usage record` over 50 runs on the dev machine in the PR (not asserted). Bump version and CHANGELOG per the phase PR. Acceptance: tests pass, typecheck and prettier clean.

tasks.subject: [flow-usage] [P2] Ship flow usage scan: backfill limit hits from transcripts, idempotently
tasks.description:
Add plugins/flow/scripts/cli/usage-scan.ts: `flow usage scan [--account <id>] [--days <n> | --all] [--dry-run] [--json]`.
- Targets: every registered identity with a valid id, or --account (unknown -> exit 5).
- Files: walk <path>/projects/ recursively for *.jsonl without following symlinks; keep files with mtime within the last --days (default 8) unless --all.
- Stream each file line by line (readline over createReadStream); JSON.parse a line only if it contains the text "rate_limit"; an unparsable line or unreadable file is a warning and scanning continues.
- Each entry -> fromTranscriptEntry (task 1.1). Count hits and unidentified. Keep the latest observation per window key per account (largest observedAt).
- Unless --dry-run, call S1's ledger writer ONCE per account with those observations. Idempotence comes from the merge rule: an equal observedAt keeps the stored entry and an unchanged ledger is not rewritten; an older observation loses to a newer stored reading.
- Human output per account: files read, hits, unidentified, and per window `recorded (limited until <local time>)` or `unchanged (a newer reading is stored)`. JSON: {v:1, days: n | 'all', accounts:[{id, files, hits, unidentified, observations, changed:[keys]}], warnings}. Exit 0.
Tests (engine-tests/usage/scan.test.ts) using the task 1.1 transcript fixtures laid out under a temp config dir's projects/<slug>/: finds the structured and text hits and skips the decoy and model-limit lines (DOR-2369 validation 2); the --days mtime filter excludes an old file and --all includes it; a second run leaves the ledger file byte-identical with the same mtime; a newer statusline reading already stored is not overwritten; --dry-run writes nothing; a torn line warns and the rest still record. Each test has a purpose comment and is shown to fail against a broken implementation. Acceptance: tests pass, typecheck and prettier clean.

tasks.subject: [flow-usage] [P2] Ship flow usage probe (one official turn, cost stated first) and the compliance guard
tasks.description:
Add plugins/flow/scripts/cli/usage-probe.ts: `flow usage probe <id> [--model <alias>] [--timeout <s>] [--claude <path>] [--yes] [--json]`.
- Unknown or invalid id: exit 5.
- Always print first (stderr in --json mode): "This runs one short Claude Code turn on <label or id> (<path>) with model <model>. It uses a small part of that account's 5-hour limit, and starts a new 5-hour window if none is running. It sends no files and allows no tools." Without --yes add "Run again with --yes to go ahead." and exit 0 without running anything.
- Binary: --claude, else FLOW_CLAUDE_BIN, else `claude` on PATH; not found -> exit 3 naming what was tried.
- Env: current env plus CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<account path>, with these REMOVED (never read): ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY. Keep the list as one exported const PROBE_STRIPPED_ENV.
- Args as an array (no shell): ['-p', 'Reply with the single word OK.', '--model', model (default 'haiku'), '--output-format', 'stream-json', '--verbose', '--tools', '', '--strict-mcp-config', '--no-session-persistence', '--settings', '{"disableAllHooks":true}']. NEVER --bare (bare mode signs in with an API key only, so it would not read the subscription's limits). cwd = a fresh mkdtemp folder, removed afterwards.
- Timeout --timeout seconds (default 90): SIGTERM the child by its pid, SIGKILL 5 s later, exit 5.
- Parse stdout NDJSON: system/init with apiKeySource other than 'none' -> stop the child, exit 5 "this account answered with an API key (<apiKeySource>), not its subscription; nothing recorded"; rate_limit_event -> fromRateLimitEvent(line.rate_limit_info, now) (task 1.1), source sdk_event; result -> done; non-JSON line -> warning.
- One ledger writer call with all observations; exit 0 when at least one recorded; none -> exit 5 "the probe finished but reported no usage; nothing recorded"; spawn failure exit 3. Human: one line per recorded window. JSON: {v:1, account, model, observations, changed, apiKeySource}.

Add engine-tests/usage/compliance-guard.test.ts: fail if any file under scripts/fleet/, scripts/usage/, scripts/cli/usage*.ts or scripts/cli/fleet.ts contains `oauth/usage`, `find-generic-password`, `Keychain`, `.credentials.json` or `api.anthropic.com`; fail if any of them reads the VALUE of CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (the PROBE_STRIPPED_ENV const is the one allowed mention, found by name); fail if `fetch(` appears outside fleet/sessions.ts. Prove it by adding a violating line to a temp copy and watching it fail.

Tests (engine-tests/usage/probe.test.ts) with a fake process runner: without --yes the runner is never called and the note prints; with --yes the runner receives exactly the args above, env has CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and none of the removed vars, cwd is a temp dir that no longer exists afterwards; a scripted stream with two rate_limit_event lines records both as sdk_event with utilization x 100; apiKeySource 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' exits 5 and records nothing; no event exits 5; a hanging child is killed at the timeout. Acceptance: tests pass, typecheck and prettier clean.

tasks.subject: [flow-usage] [P2] Ship flow usage install-statusline: add the two lines per account, only with --yes
tasks.description:
Add plugins/flow/scripts/cli/usage-install.ts: `flow usage install-statusline [--account <id>] [--yes] [--remove] [--json]`.
- Targets: every registered identity with a valid id, or --account (unknown -> exit 5).
- Find the script: read <path>/settings.json; need statusLine.type 'command' and a string statusLine.command of the form `<script>` or `bash|sh|zsh <script>`, the script optionally single- or double-quoted and optionally starting with ~/, $HOME/ or ${HOME}/ (expanded); it must be an existing regular file. The script needs a line matching /^\s*(?:local\s+)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=["']?\$\(cat\)["']?\s*(#.*)?$/; the first match gives <var>. Anything else is `manual` with a reason (no status line, inline command, not a file, no capture line) and the two lines printed with a placeholder variable.
- The block = the marker comment line starting `# flow usage recorder` plus the hook line directly after it:
  `# flow usage recorder (opt-in): records this account's usage for \`flow fleet\`. See <flow-root>/docs/account-usage.mdx`
  `[ -x '<H>' ] && { printf '%s' "$<var>" | FLOW_NODE='<N>' '<H>'; } >/dev/null 2>&1 &`
  H = realpath of <flowRoot>/scripts/usage/statusline-hook.sh; N = process.execPath. Either containing a single quote or newline -> exit 5; the hook not executable -> exit 5 naming it.
- Plan: block absent -> insert after the capture line; present and identical -> none; present with other paths -> update in place; --remove with block -> remove, without -> none.
- Without --yes: print each plan (script, action, line number, exact lines), write nothing, exit 0 (5 if any target is manual).
- With --yes, per insert/update/remove: copy the script to <script>.flow-backup-<epoch ms>; write the new text to a temp file in the same folder with the original mode; rename over the script; re-read and verify the block appears exactly once (or zero times after remove), else restore the backup and exit 5. Preserve every other byte: line endings (LF or CRLF) and the presence or absence of a final newline. Never write settings.json.
- Human: one line per account (e.g. `claude3  inserted after line 4 of /.../statusline-command.sh (backup: ...)`). JSON: {v:1, accounts:[{id, script|null, action, reason?, line?, lines?, applied, backup?}]}.
Tests (engine-tests/usage/install-statusline.test.ts) on temp config dirs: without --yes every script is byte-identical afterwards; --yes inserts after the capture line (a fixture modeled on a real status-line script that starts with `input=$(cat)`); a second run is none; changed paths are updated; --remove restores the original bytes exactly, including CRLF and no-final-newline fixtures; each manual reason; settings.json unchanged in every case; a path with a quote exits 5. Each test has a purpose comment and is shown to fail against a broken implementation. Acceptance: tests pass, typecheck and prettier clean.

tasks.subject: [flow-usage] [P2] Ship flow fleet: accounts with bars and countdowns, sessions with account, item, state and host, read-only
tasks.description:
Add plugins/flow/scripts/fleet/render.ts (pure) and plugins/flow/scripts/cli/fleet.ts, registered in flow.ts: `flow fleet [--project <dir>] [--dorkos-url <url> | --no-dorkos] [--json]`. Needs no flow project config and no tracker. Writes NOTHING: no file, lock, stamp or tracker; the only network call is one GET to a loopback DorkOS (task 1.2).
- Accounts: S1 readIdentities in registry order with readFleetPolicy; for valid ids every ledger window through readWindow(entry, now), effectiveReservePct, fiveHourRoom, weeklyRoom; lastSeen = newest observedAt.
- Sessions: readCliSessions + fetchDorkosSessions (skipped with --no-dorkos) + collectRuns over --project (default cwd) and every distinct session cwd, joined by joinSessions/sessionState (task 1.2).
- Human output, plain, aligned, uncolored, at most 100 columns for ids up to 12 chars:
```
Accounts                  5-hour                     week
  claude2  main      [####......]  41%  2h 14m   [#######...]  72%  3d 04h   reserve 50%, seen 3m ago
  claude3  rotation  [##########]  out  0h 42m   [###.......]  31%  5d 11h   limited (5-hour), seen 1h ago
  claude4  kept-out  no reading                  [..........]   0%  reset    seen 6d ago

Sessions
  claude2  DOR-2369  busy     cli     1a2b3c4d  ~/…/marketplace/spec-flow-usage  3h
  claude3  -         limited  cli     9f8e7d6c  ~/Keep/dork-os/dorkos            12m
  claude2  DOR-2370  unseen   dorkos  5e4d3c2b  -                                -

DorkOS: not running at http://127.0.0.1:4242
```
  Bar: 10 cells, '#' = round(usedPct/10), '.' empty. Percent: rounded usedPct; 'out' when status rejected; '0%' when expired. Countdown: '<1m', '42m', '2h 14m', '3d 04h'; 'reset' when expired; '-' when resetsAt null. A window with no reading prints 'no reading'. Notes in order: 'reserve N%' for a non-zero reserve ('reserve N% (0% now: spend-down)' inside the spend-down window); 'limited (5-hour|week)'; 'kept out of all repos' for kept-out with no scope; 'seen <age> ago'. An invalid-id row shows 'invalid id, not tracked'. Session cells: account id ('?' unknown), item ('-'), state, host ('?' unknown), first 8 chars of sessionId, cwd with home as ~ cut from the left to 34 chars with '…', age since startedAt ('-'). No accounts: 'No accounts registered. Add one: flow accounts add --path ~/.claude'. No sessions: 'Sessions: none running'. Footer always: 'Sessions on accounts flow does not know are not shown.' DorkOS note: 'DorkOS: not running at <url>' or 'DorkOS: running, but it does not report live sessions yet' (reportsLive false). Warnings to stderr.
- JSON: {v:1, now, handoff, accounts:[{id, label, color, path, validId, role, reservePct, effectiveReservePct, scopeRepos, fiveHourRoom, weeklyRoom, lastSeen, windows:{<key>:{usedPct, resetsAt, status, observedAt, source, expired}}}], sessions:[{sessionId, account, item, stage, state, host, pid, cwd, startedAt, sources}], dorkos:{url, reachable, reportsLive}, warnings}. Stale windows are absent; expired ones carry expired:true and usedPct 0.
- Exit 0; 2 for argv errors and a non-loopback URL.
Tests (engine-tests/fleet/render.test.ts, fleet.test.ts): a golden text for a fixed now covering expired, stale, rejected, no reading, spend-down, an invalid id, an unknown account and every session state, every line <= 100 columns; the three sources joined so a session serving an item shows it (DOR-2370 validations 1 and 2); the JSON shape; READ-ONLY: snapshot path, size, mtime and bytes of the temp DORK_HOME, the config dirs and the project before and after -> identical, and the fake fetch saw exactly one GET (DOR-2370 validation 3); DorkOS refused, 401 and pre-D7 bodies give their note or warning; a non-loopback URL exits 2. Each test has a purpose comment and is shown to fail against a broken implementation. Acceptance: tests pass, typecheck and prettier clean.

tasks.subject: [flow-usage] [P3] Document account usage and prove the recorder, scan, probe and fleet live on the operator's machine
tasks.description:
Docs, written with the writing-for-humans skill (plain enough for a smart 9th grader; no hype; never describe it as a way to get more out of a plan; call it account-aware scheduling):
- New plugins/flow/docs/account-usage.mdx, added to docs/meta.json after parallel-drain: what flow records (each account's 5-hour and weekly use and reset times), where (<dork home>/usage/<id>.json), and from where (the status line, transcripts, an official probe turn; never the Keychain, never a usage endpoint); the two status-line lines and `flow usage install-statusline` (nothing changes without --yes; a backup is kept; --remove undoes it); `flow usage scan`; `flow usage probe` and its cost (a small part of the 5-hour limit, and it starts a 5-hour window if none is running); how to read the `flow fleet` screen (bars, out, reset, no reading, the session states busy, idle, parked, limited, stale, unseen); and the note that each person must judge their own use against Anthropic's terms and that flow is built for one person's own accounts.
- README.md verb table gains `usage` and `fleet`; docs/SPEC.md CLI surface gains both verbs.
- CHANGELOG entry and version bump in plugin.json, .dork/manifest.json and package.json.
Live proof on the operator's machine (paste the output into the PR, with home paths shortened to ~):
1. `flow usage install-statusline` without --yes for every registered account (shows the plan, changes nothing).
2. `--yes --account <one rotation account>`, then use that account interactively for one reply and confirm <dork home>/usage/<id>.json has five_hour and seven_day with resetsAt.
3. `flow usage scan` (reports the hits found).
4. `flow usage probe <one account> --yes` once, and record whether a rate_limit_event arrived (assumption A8). If it did not, say so in the PR; the verb's honest exit 5 stands.
